claim: AW25 / A-051 (analytics walk 2026-10-03), founder pick 2026-10-04 ~00:30Z, verbatim "Learn from the POS (Recommended)". Migration tables_learned_from_the_pos (cited by slug, ADR 0235) gives pos_checks a table_ref column holding the till's word, makes restaurant_tables.seats nullable and adds learned_at and hidden_at. A BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF raw, table_id, table_ref trigger on pos_checks (no WHEN clause: it reads the word out of raw first) resolves the word against the house's tables and learns a table when none answers and the word has an ASCII digit in it (founder, 2026-10-05 ~14:15Z, verbatim "Only words with a number (Recommended)"): 'T12', '12', 'Patio 3' are learned, while 'booth' or 'Ayla' keeps its table_ref, links only to a table that already answers it, and makes none. A word longer than 60 characters, the most PATCH lets a person name a table, keeps its table_ref and makes none either (2026-10-05, fix list after the afda5d868 BLOCK); the check is stored, never refused. The backfill runs the same trigger, so history follows the same rule. A DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED constraint trigger re-links earlier unlinked checks to a learned table at commit, and both re-link UPDATEs (the immediate one after a person adds, renames, re-maps or re-activates a table, and the deferred one after learning) fill only rows with table_id IS NULL, so a re-link never moves a link. The backfill copies the word out of raw for history. Evidence: supabase/tests/<ver>_tables_learned_from_the_pos_test.sql T1-T29 on the local Postgres harness (T19 and T20 pin the never-moves rule, one per re-link UPDATE, and since 2026-10-05 also that the re-link leaves a linked row unwritten (its ctid), because the trigger's own belt would hold the link anyway; T29 pins the 60-character cap; T21-T23 pin the digit rule for new checks, the backfill, and an owner-added 'Bar' that links past and new 'bar' checks) (pgtest.sh lane, p4-scratch/sim-run/fixes/audits/tables-local-pg.txt). The check fails if the migration goes, if any of these clauses goes, or if a later migration drops the learning trigger without re-creating it. Mutation-checked 2026-10-04 against main 1aa4dcb8c (fails), by deleting the deferred trigger clause (fails) and by dropping raw from the trigger's column list (fails); 2026-10-05 by removing c.table_id IS NULL from either re-link UPDATE (fails), and by removing the digit test from the learning condition (fails; it also fails on b440d85fa, the head before the digit rule). 2026-10-05 (after the afda5d868 BLOCK): fails at afda5d868 (no length cap in the learning condition) and when the cap is removed; the SQL test fails (T29) when the cap is removed.

claim: Founder, 2026-10-05 (asked ~23:22Z on the afda5d868 BLOCK), verbatim pick "Keep every spelling (Recommended)": "A table remembers every till spelling it was ever linked by, not just one. A rename never creates a twin table, and past checks never move." Migration tables_learned_from_the_pos (cited by slug, ADR 0235) adds restaurant_tables.till_words (jsonb {source: [word, ...]}, NOT NULL, default empty) and former_labels (text[], NOT NULL, default empty). restaurant_tables_keep_till_names fires BEFORE UPDATE OF label, pos_refs when either changes: it adds every distinct word (GROUP BY source and word, no DISTINCT ON) on a check linked to the row, per source, and the row's earlier pos_refs words to till_words, and the old label to former_labels, dropping nothing already kept. pos_table_for_ref reads both last (rank 3: a till word of that source, or a former label by the label and "table <label>" rules), so a renamed or re-mapped table answers what it answered before and the learner, which learns only when nothing answers, makes no twin. pos_checks_find_or_learn_table holds a past check where it is: an update that leaves the check's word as it was keeps OLD.table_id whatever the statement sets (the belt). claim: AW25 and fix round 1 of lane tables (2026-10-04): the till's table word reaches pos_checks.table_ref through the database, not the gateway. pos_checks_find_or_learn_table (migration tables_learned_from_the_pos) sets table_ref from public.pos_table_ref_from_raw(source, raw) on every insert and on every update that writes raw: a word raw carries wins, a word that came from the old raw goes when the new raw names none, and a changed word re-resolves a link the statement did not set itself. pos-hub.service.ts therefore writes no table_ref (its row literal is main's), so a gateway deployed before the migration still stores every check, and the gateway already running learns tables as soon as the migration applies.
